blocks.html: This guideline now covers both SAPUI5 and SAP Web Components. Learn More.

Expandable text is a UI component that displays long text in a collapsed or expanded state. By default, it shows a short preview with a Show More link to reveal the full content and a Show Less link to collapse it again. Depending on the use case, the text can expand inline or open in a popover.

blocks.alt: An expandable text in the collapsed state, showing 'The request includes read access to the financial reporting module and write access to...' followed by a 'Show More' link.

blocks.html: This component is available in the following libraries:

• Choose inline expansion when space allows and the surrounding context helps users understand the full text.
  • Choose expanded in popover mode when inline expansion would disrupt the layout.
  • Set the character limit based on the use case. For example, a form and a list row may need very different thresholds.
  • Rewrite the text instead of relying on truncation whenever it can be shortened without losing meaning.
  • Use expandable text only for optional details. If users need the full content to complete a task, show it by default.

items.html:
Use the expandable text to:

  • Handle long texts or descriptions inside a responsive table, list or form.
  • Provide access to truncated text.

Don't use the expandable text to:

  • Handle text overflow in UI tables (grid table, tree table, analytical table) or the Gantt chart.
  • Display content for which a short and meaningful alternative exists.
  • Hide only non-critical content. Use short descriptions that fit into the available space instead.

blocks.html: The expandable text consists of the following elements:

1. Main text: The truncated content displayed when the component is in its collapsed state.
  2. Popover with expanded text: A floating container that displays the full text content. The popover can include an arrow pointer on any of its four sides.
  3. Expand/collapse link: A Show More/Show Less link that expands or collapses the component.

Note: The Show More/Show Less link labels are predefined and cannot be changed. Translations are handled automatically by the component.

The enabled state is the default state of the expandable text.

blocks.caption: Enabled state of the expandable text
blocks.alt: An expandable text in the enabled component state, showing the full paragraph text ending with '...revealed only when the user needs more context.' followed by a 'Show Less' link.

blocks.html:
The expandable text component inherits the interaction states for the Show More/Show Less link only.

A. Regular: The default state of the link.

B. Hover: Displayed when the cursor moves over the link.

C. Down: Displayed while the link is being activated.

blocks.caption: For more information, see Interaction States.
blocks.alt: Three expandable text items labeled A–C showing truncated text. B displays an underlined "Show More" link, while A and C do not.

blocks.html:
The focus state indicates the element that currently has keyboard focus. In the expandable text component, focus is applied to the Show More/Show Less link only.

A. Unfocused: The default state of the link when it has not received focus.

B. Focused: Displayed when the link receives focus, visualized with a focus highlight around it.

blocks.caption: For more information, see Focus state.
blocks.alt: Two expandable text items labeled A and B, each showing truncated text. B displays a blue focus outline around the "Show More" link, while A does not.

blocks.html: Display an en dash (–) to denote empty content and make values easier to scan in forms and similar contexts.  The symbol may vary depending on the user's language.

blocks.alt: A responsive table with columns 'Product', 'Attribute 1', and 'Attribute 2': 'Product 1' shows truncated text 'This is a product description. It provides supplementary information about the item without taking...' in the Attribute 1 column, while 'Product 2' shows a dash (–) indicating no content.

blocks.html: For more information, see Empty States.
The expandable text expands either inline or in a popover. Clicking Show More reveals the full content. The text is selectable and the user can copy it in both collapsed and expanded modes.

blocks.alt: Two interaction steps labeled A and B: (A) a collapsed Expandable Text showing truncated text '...without taking... Show More', and (B) the same text expanded in place showing the full paragraph followed by a 'Show Less' link.

blocks.html: Collapsed (A) and expanded in place (B)
Clicking Show Less or outside the popover collapses the text.

blocks.alt: Two interaction steps labeled C and D: (C) a collapsed Expandable Text showing truncated text '...without taking... Show More', and (D) a popover appearing alongside the text displaying the full paragraph ending with '...revealed only when the user needs more context.'

blocks.html: Collapsed (C) and expanded in popover (D)
The behavior is similar to mouse interaction.
For more information, see Gestures.

blocks.html: For more information, see Content Density.

The expandable text is responsive and supports all screen sizes. It does not change size between compact and cozy content densities.

 The expandable text supports inline and popover expansion on all screen sizes. On mobile, popovers don't float, they open as a full-screen overlay, making it easier to read and interact with the content.

SAP follows international standards, such as WCAG and WAI-ARIA, and strives to make our business solutions accessible and inclusive. For more information, see Accessibility in SAP Fiori and the Accessibility Design Tools Handbook.
Keyboard interaction is supported through the Show More / Show Less link, which follows the keyboard behavior of the Link component.

Screen readers read plain text through the virtual cursor, also known as browse mode or the virtual PC cursor.

Plain text cannot receive keyboard focus, so users do not navigate to it using the Tab key. Instead, screen reader users read plain text using commands that move by line, word, character, heading, list, or section.

The expandable text wraps and truncates according to the available space. Text exceeding 100 characters is truncated and followed by a Show More link.

A. More than 100 characters: Text truncates and shows a Show More link.

B. Less than 100 characters: Text is displayed in full and no Show More link.

blocks.caption: Truncation in the expandable text
blocks.alt: Two expandable text items labeled A and B: (A) shows truncated text '...without taking...' followed by a 'Show More' link, and (B) shows the shorter complete text 'This is a product description. It provides supplementary information.' with no expand link.

blocks.html:
When hyphenation is enabled, it affects both the collapsed and expanded states.

A. Collapsed mode with hyphenation: Text truncates and shows a Show More link.

B. Expanded in popover with hyphenation: The full content in the popover is displayed with hyphenation.

blocks.caption: Collapsed with hyphenation (A) and expanded in a popover with hyphenation (B)
blocks.alt: Two expandable text items labeled A and B: (A) shows collapsed text with a 'Show More' link, and (B) shows the same collapsed text alongside an open popover displaying the full paragraph ending with '...revealed only when the user needs more context.'

blocks.html: For more information, see Wrapping & Truncation  and Wrapping and Truncating Text.
The expandable text supports left-to-right (LTR) and right-to-left (RTL) reading directions. All features are supported in both directions.
